easy.q: According to Elder Matthew J. Eyring, who knows exactly how we feel, even in our darkest and hardest times?
options: Only people with the same trial
Our Savior, Jesus Christ
Our very closest friends
easy.why: Elder Eyring taught that the Savior suffered for us: “He knows exactly how we feel, especially in our darkest and most trying times.”

easy.q: Elder Matthew J. Eyring told of a friend who received very sad news about his family. What single thought came to the friend's mind?
options: “I can’t fix this.”
“I must stay strong.”
“I need a plan.”
easy.why: The friend's thought was “I can’t fix this.” Elder Eyring used it to teach that all of us will meet burdens we cannot carry by ourselves.

easy.q: After dinner with a young couple who were grieving, what did Elder Matthew J. Eyring have the opportunity to give the father?
options: A letter of advice
A book of scripture
A priesthood blessing
easy.why: The mother had received a blessing in the hospital, but the father had not, so Elder Eyring gave him a priesthood blessing after their dinner together.

easy.q: At the end of his talk, which promise of the Savior did Elder Matthew J. Eyring invite us to believe and find comfort in?
options: He will take away every hard thing
He will not leave us comfortless
He will tell us all the reasons now
easy.why: Elder Eyring closed with the Savior's promise: “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.”

easy.q: What did Elder Matthew J. Eyring say should be one of our highest priorities?
options: Learning to handle every problem by ourselves
Staying away from every hardship in life
Living worthy to have the Holy Ghost always with us
easy.why: He taught that the Savior's peace comes through the Holy Ghost, so living worthy of His “constant companionship” should be one of our highest priorities.

medium.q: Why did Elder Matthew J. Eyring begin his talk with a friend's thought, “I can’t fix this”?
options: To teach that we should give up trying to solve problems
To show that strong faith keeps sorrow away from us
To show that all of us will meet burdens we cannot carry alone
To warn that hard times come mostly to the unprepared
medium.why: Elder Eyring said our apparent self-reliance masks a deeper reality: all of us “will sooner or later encounter burdens we cannot possibly carry ourselves.”

medium.q: What allowed Elder Matthew J. Eyring and his wife to offer special empathy to the young couple they joined for dinner?
options: They had passed through a similar loss many years before
They had known the couple since the two were children
They had been trained to counsel families in sorrow
They had been assigned to minister to the couple's ward
medium.why: Elder Eyring said he and his wife expressed “empathy gained through our own suffering,” grateful to mourn with those who mourn and comfort those in need of comfort.

medium.q: According to Elder Matthew J. Eyring, what is one reason we will not survive spiritually in coming days without the constant influence of the Holy Ghost?
options: The scriptures will become much harder to understand
True sources of comfort will become more scarce
Prophets will give counsel far less often than now
Members will gather for worship less and less often
medium.why: He taught that “in a world of increasing temporal and spiritual turbulence, true sources of comfort will become more scarce.” The Holy Ghost is the Comforter we will need.

medium.q: Elder Matthew J. Eyring said the Lord spares us from “the only two things” that can bring us permanent misery. What are they?
options: Lasting poverty and deep loneliness throughout this life
Prayers that go unanswered and trials left unexplained
Failing health and the loss of the people we love most
Separation from our bodies and separation from God because of sin
medium.why: Elder Eyring named them: “separation from our bodies and separation from God because of sin.” Even as the Lord comforts us in temporary pain, He has prepared our rescue from permanent tragedy.

medium.q: Elder Matthew J. Eyring said the Lord's answers come by various means as guided by the Spirit. In what form did he say they sometimes come?
options: An immediate end to the trial we are facing
Tools, resources, and help from other people
Greater willpower to carry the burden alone
A clear explanation of why the trial came
medium.why: He taught that answers come “sometimes in the form of tools, resources, and help from other people.” The Lord often answers through means He places around us.

hard.q: Elder Matthew J. Eyring described what can happen step by step when we lack divine comfort. In his sequence, what do we risk losing first?
options: Our faith
Our hope
Our testimony
Our will to try
hard.why: The order matters: “Without divine comfort, we risk losing hope; and without hope, we can lose our faith and stop trying.” Comfort protects hope, and hope protects faith.

hard.q: According to Elder Matthew J. Eyring, what will we someday realize about all the suffering that brought us closer to the Savior?
options: It could have been avoided with more effort
It was the result of our own weak faith
It was preparing us for greater blessings
It was never meant to be fully understood
hard.why: He taught: “We will realize that all the suffering that brought us closer to the Savior was preparing us for greater blessings.”

hard.q: Elder Matthew J. Eyring spoke of temporary times of challenge and pain and of permanent tragedy. Which statement best explains what he said the Lord does about each?
options: He removes the temporary now so that we need not fear the permanent
He allows the temporary only for those who have risked the permanent
He explains the temporary now and saves His comfort for the permanent
He comforts us through the temporary and has prepared rescue from the permanent
hard.why: Elder Eyring taught, “Even as He comforts us through temporary times of challenge and pain, He has prepared our rescue from permanent tragedy.” The pain is comforted, not removed; death and sin are overcome.

hard.q: Which situation best fits what Elder Matthew J. Eyring taught about times when we can't fix things on our own?
options: A mother's trial continues, but she turns to the Lord and feels peace through the Spirit
A father decides that needing help with his trial shows that his faith is too weak
A student waits to pray until she has first solved her problem by herself
A man concludes that because his trial has not ended, the Lord has forgotten him
hard.why: Elder Eyring taught that the Savior's peace comes through the Holy Ghost, and that this comfort helps us through hardships and “times when we can’t fix things on our own.”

hard.q: A woman has prayed for months about a heavy trial. Which expectation best fits what Elder Matthew J. Eyring promised those who cast their burdens on the Lord?
options: An answer will come as soon as her faith is strong enough to deserve one
Comfort will come only after she understands why the trial was given
Comfort will come, and answers in His time, perhaps through other people
Answers will come to her directly, without tools or help from anyone else
hard.why: He promised, “He will provide comfort; He will provide answers on His timetable as you turn to Him,” and said answers sometimes come as tools, resources, and help from other people.
